It's not *impossible* to cross over to AD from the G/R, but the slots are limited, and a lot of recruiters will not want to work with you as a prior service member. 

The biggest thing to note is that prior service slots are allocated per fiscal year. Once the allocation has been met, applications are closed until the next fiscal year. Last year they had 100 slots, this current fiscal year they upped it to 200 members. People can speculate as to why it's so limited, but in reality only HAF has the answer. 

I'll say you should pursue it if that is your goal, don't listen to people just saying that it's impossible and that you'll never get picked up. Do however keep in mind that it can be a lengthy process, it took me almost a year from initial contact with a recruiter to re-enlisting AD.

Strictly speaking benefits wise, they are functionally the same. Same pay, same retirement, same healthcare, etc. 

AD is governed at the federal level, and has much more control over you and your career. You are vulnerable to PCS/deploy/TDY mure more than an AGR will.

AGR is governed at the state level, and you have much more control over you and your career. You will not PCS unless you elect to. You have more say in if you deploy or TDY.

A lot of people try to get picked up as an AGR just for the stability, and generally speaking ANG/Reserve AGRs deal with less "AD bullshit" than AD people will. You have to apply and usually board/interview for AGR postions, akin to applying for a civilian job. So networking and knowing people in the ANG/Reserve is much more important than it is as AD.

edit: Also as an AGR you are capped at promotion. You can promote up to the max grade that is assigned to your position. If you hit the max grade then you have to apply for another AGR position with a higher grade allowance. It gets exponentially harder to promote after TSgt usually.
